title: Judicial Pardon
definition: Judicial Pardon is God's legal forgiveness of the believer's guilt on the basis of Christ's finished work.
summary: Judicial Pardon emphasizes God's legal declaration that the believer is no longer condemned.
christFocus: Jesus Christ secures pardon by bearing sin and standing as the believer's advocate.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Judicial pardon is God's legal forgiveness of the guilty through Christ. Scripture presents sin as guilt before the holy Judge, not merely sickness, weakness, or social failure.

In pardon, God does not deny justice. He forgives because Christ has borne judgment, satisfied righteousness, and provided a just basis for mercy.

Jesus stands at the center of this doctrine as the condemned substitute and risen advocate. Because of Him, the guilty can be declared pardoned rather than condemned.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Judicial pardon matters because people need more than emotional relief; they need a real answer to guilt before God. This doctrine corrects the idea that forgiveness is God simply overlooking sin.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your guilt to God through Christ instead of minimizing it. Thank Him for a pardon that is legally secure, and let that mercy make you honest, humble, and merciful toward others.
